title: Jitsonville Pack
description: A vanilla++ client-focused pack for the Jitsonville server, emphasizing fresh visuals, resource packs, QoL tweaks, and performance.
body:
# Jitsonville Pack

**Jitsonville Pack** is a **vanilla / vanilla+** modpack built specifically for the associated **Jitsonville server**, with a focus on making the game feel **cleaner, smoother, and more alive** without changing the core Minecraft experience.

This pack is primarily **client-side** and prioritizes **visual upgrades, performance improvements, and quality-of-life features**, with only a small amount of **light content** (such as simple farming enhancements) to keep gameplay familiar.

---

## What this modpack focuses on

### Vanilla+ visuals (main focus)
- A large set of curated **resource packs** designed to **freshen and diversify** Minecraft’s look  
- Subtle visual polish intended to make the world feel **cleaner and more cohesive**.

### Quality of life improvements
- Practical UI and usability mods to reduce friction while staying true to vanilla pacing  
- Better readability, convenience features, and small enhancements that make everyday play more enjoyable

### Performance and stability
- Performance mods selected to improve **FPS**, reduce stutter, and keep the pack lightweight  
- Chosen for compatibility and stability in a multiplayer environment

### Light content additions (kept minimal)
- A few small, low-impact mods (ex: farming-related improvements) that fit naturally into vanilla gameplay  
- No heavy progression overhaul just extra polish and a little variety

---

## Intended use

This pack is designed for the **Jitsonville server** first. It may work elsewhere, but the best experience is on the server it was built for, where settings and compatibility are already aligned.

---

## Compatibility notes

- Recommended to use the pack **as-is** for best stability.
- Adding additional mods or resource packs may cause conflicts, especially with visuals and performance.

---

## Credits

All mods and resource packs belong to their respective authors. Any required attributions are included in the project description or version changelog where applicable.
